clue.text: Where writers come to fisticuffs ?

parts.note: journalists collectively are the press
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A place where authors end up brawling.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a place for brawling authors; 'Where' alone defines the enclosure at a stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the reserved area at a stadium where journalists sit to report on the game.

clue.text: "Getting and spending, we lay waste our ——" (Wordsworth)

definitions.text: "Getting and spending, we lay waste our ——" (Wordsworth)

parts.words: Getting and spending, we lay waste our ——" (Wordsworth)
parts.note: a line from Wordsworth's sonnet The World Is Too Much With Us, with its last word left as a gap to fill

explanation.surface: A quotation from Wordsworth with its final word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank: the sonnet line ends 'we lay waste our powers'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word of the poem means our faculties or abilities, which the poet says we squander on commerce.

clue.text: Quality of the Just So Stories?

definitions.text: Quality of the Just So Stories?

parts.words: Quality of the Just So Stories?
parts.note: Kipling's book title is read literally: 'just so' means precisely right, so the quality is precision

explanation.surface: A question about the character of Kipling's children's tales.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's Just So Stories is read as 'stories that are just so', i.e. exactly right.
explanation.definitionFit: Being 'just so' is being precise, and precision is the quality named.

clue.text: Old musical rounds

parts.note: ancient astronomy held that the heavenly globes made a music as they turned; 'rounds' looks like sung canons

explanation.surface: Some antique songs sung as canons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rounds' suggests songs like Frère Jacques; here it means round bodies, the crystal globes of old astronomy that were said to make music.
explanation.definitionFit: The 'music of the spheres' was the harmony the ancients believed the heavenly orbs produced.

clue.text: Go up with the old thing, there are bad men about

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word go is written bottom to top

parts.note: res is Latin for a thing, the language of old

explanation.surface: Some advice to climb with an antique, since villains are lurking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns Go in a down entry; 'the old thing' is Latin, the language of antiquity. 'there are' and 'about' only join the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Monsters of fairy tale, these are cruel, brutish figures.

clue.text: Two hands of fruit ?

indicators.note: two of the following word are wanted, so it is written twice

parts.note: a paw is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: Two handfuls of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical fruit, another name for the papaya.

clue.text: Makes an end of hopeful travelling

definitions.text: Makes an end of hopeful travelling

parts.words: Makes an end of hopeful travelling
parts.note: Stevenson wrote that to travel hopefully is better than to reach your goal, so this is what ends the hopeful journey

explanation.surface: Someone brings their optimistic journey to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: R. L. Stevenson: 'To travel hopefully is a better thing than to arrive.' Reaching the destination ends the hopeful travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching one's destination is what finishes any journey.

clue.text: Music first

parts.note: in Italian musical terms the first or upper part of a duet is so marked

explanation.surface: Putting music ahead of everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: In a piano duet the upper part is marked with the Italian word for 'first'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Italian word for first, used in scores for the leading part.

clue.text: Scoldings that can effect transformations ?

explanation.surface: Telling-offs that change people for the better.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'transformation' was an old word for a wig, so fittings of wigs effect transformations.
explanation.definitionFit: A wigging is a severe telling-off; and wig fittings transform a person's look, a hairpiece once being called a transformation.

clue.text: A powerful passage of literature ?

parts.note: C. P. Snow's novel title The ... of Power is read as a passage that is powerful

explanation.surface: A forceful excerpt from a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage of literature' suggests an extract; it is a hallway from C. P. Snow's novel Corridors of Power.
explanation.definitionFit: A long passage in a building, here the one of power from C. P. Snow's title.

clue.text: Overlapping in the building world ?

parts.note: builders clad walls with horizontal planks that overlap one another

explanation.surface: Some duplication of effort in the construction trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlapping' suggests duplication; it is literal: exterior planks laid so each covers the edge of the one below.
explanation.definitionFit: This cladding uses horizontal boards that overlap to shed rain from a wall.

clue.text: Concerned with injuries in the lab?

definitions.note: the definition points to vessels found in a laboratory, a plural noun

parts.note: re means concerning or about
torts are civil wrongs or injuries in law

explanation.surface: Studying wounds in a laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Injuries' is the legal sense: a tort is a civil wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: These are glass vessels with long necks used for distilling in a laboratory.

clue.text: Right, Olivia will get the pasta

indicators.note: the letters of the name will get a new order, rearranged into a different form

explanation.surface: Olivia is going to be served the pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will get' is the anagram signal on the name Olivia; the surface makes it sound like she is being served.
explanation.definitionFit: Small stuffed pasta squares, an Italian dish.

clue.text: Sized up and certain to be found in the field

indicators.note: one word is found inside the other, so it goes in the middle

parts.note: mead is a poetic word for a meadow or field
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Assessed and sure to be out on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Mead is a poetic, old word for a meadow, which a solver reading 'field' may not think of.
explanation.definitionFit: To size something up is to gauge its dimensions, i.e. to take its measurements.

clue.text: Tame leaders of the dawn chorus

definitions.text: Tame leaders of the dawn chorus

parts.words: Tame leaders of the dawn chorus
parts.note: domestic farmyard birds are the first to crow at daybreak

explanation.surface: Gentle conductors of the birdsong at sunrise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tame' is domesticated, and these farmyard males are the first to call at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Male domestic fowl, cocks, crow at dawn.

clue.text: Chuck over the arm-rest

explanation.surface: Throwing something over the arm of a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm-rest' looks like part of a chair; it is the bandage that supports an injured arm.
explanation.definitionFit: To chuck is to throw or hurl; and a support for an injured arm is a hanging bandage looped round the neck.

clue.text: Do mirages change into symbols ?

indicators.note: the letters of the two words change into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A question whether mirages turn into signs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges DO MIRAGES; 'into' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Characters that stand for ideas rather than sounds, like Chinese characters.

clue.text: A certain dear French man on the roof

parts.note: 'that' points to a certain one, as in 'that man'
cher is French for dear

explanation.surface: A particular beloved Frenchman sits on the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: THAT (a certain one) plus CHER (French for dear).
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who lays straw or reed roofing works up on the roof.

clue.text: He prophesied a whirlwind harvest

parts.note: an Old Testament prophet wrote 'they have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind'

explanation.surface: Someone foretold a sudden, rapid harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whirlwind harvest' reads as a fast one; it is the Bible verse about reaping the whirlwind.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor prophet of the Old Testament whose book holds the line about sowing the wind.

clue.text: Granted by word of mouth, we hear

indicators.note: signals that what follows is heard, a word sounding like the entry

parts.note: spoken, i.e. said out loud

explanation.surface: Permission given orally, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by word of mouth' gives ALOUD, which 'we hear' as a word meaning granted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something granted is permitted.

clue.text: Advances where bull might be expected ?

definitions.text: Advances where bull might be expected ?

parts.words: Advances where bull might be expected ?
parts.note: the reed called a bulrush has 'bul' at the front, so a word starting 'on' instead swaps that opening

explanation.surface: Charges forward at the point where a bull would appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bull' suggests a charging animal; it is the start of BULRUSHES, replaced by ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Onrushes are forward surges or charges.

clue.text: The main pursuer of Antigonus in exit ?

definitions.text: The main pursuer of Antigonus in exit ?

parts.words: The main pursuer of Antigonus in exit ?
parts.note: in The Winter's Tale Antigonus leaves the stage with the direction 'Exit, pursued by a bear'; the main is the sea

explanation.surface: Who chased Antigonus off stage in Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the sea, and the Winter's Tale's famous stage direction supplies the bear.
explanation.definitionFit: A marine bear-like animal, a name for the fur seal or the polar bear.

clue.text: Longwood's saint

parts.note: Longwood House was Napoleon's residence in exile on a South Atlantic island named after a saint

explanation.surface: The patron saint of a house called Longwood.
explanation.walkthrough: Longwood was Napoleon's house of exile; the island it stands on bears a saint's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The island of St Helena, in the South Atlantic, where Napoleon died at Longwood.

clue.text: Three players allowed in a rhyme

parts.note: a trio is a group of three musicians
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A trio of performers permitted to take part in a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A short French poem of eight lines using only two rhymes.

clue.text: The Giant of Dolgelly

parts.note: the Welsh mountain above Dolgellau is Cader ..., the chair of a legendary giant

explanation.surface: A huge figure from a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: Dolgelly is the old spelling of Dolgellau in Wales; Cader Idris above it is named for a legendary giant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh giant of legend whose chair is the mountain Cader Idris.

clue.text: West Riding point of view causes brawl

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for riding, a Yorkshire division
an angle is a standpoint or point of view

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire outlook leads to a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Riding was a division of Yorkshire; here it is split into W and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrangle is a noisy quarrel, a brawl.

clue.text: Black look from Highlanders ?

parts.note: the Black ___ is a famous Highland regiment, and the missing word also means look

explanation.surface: A scowl from Scottish mountain folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black look' seems a scowl; the Black Watch is a Highland regiment of the British Army, and its second word means look.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep watch is to look out, and the Black Watch is a Scottish regiment.

clue.text: Vigilant rider of Swallow

parts.note: the English outlaw who resisted the Normans rode a mare named Swallow, and his nickname means watchful

explanation.surface: An alert horseman on a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Swallow was the horse of the Anglo-Saxon rebel; his byname suggests alertness.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saxon rebel of the Fens who fought William the Conqueror, his epithet suggesting watchfulness.

clue.text: Stay in that wrecked street-car ?

indicators.note: the word is wrecked and rebuilt, its letters thrown into a new order

parts.note: Tennessee Williams's play is A Streetcar Named Desire, so that streetcar is desire

explanation.surface: Remaining aboard a crashed tram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that street-car' is the one named Desire in Tennessee Williams's play; 'wrecked' rearranges DESIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay somewhere is to live or dwell there.

clue.text: The daily is mum, but has "It "!

parts.note: a daily is a cleaning lady, also called a char
ma is another word for mum

explanation.surface: The cleaner says nothing, yet has sex appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like silent; it is mother. 'It' in quotes meant sex appeal in the 1920s.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm or magnetic appeal, the quality once called 'It'.
